codeReview.summary: Reviewed commit 2c411941 against the current combined code (HEAD 661d65a5) for all four items, plus their interaction with the later UI commit 5e7c5b12 (which completed the App swap/move prompt and the Sites shared-schema contract test). (1) Trailing slash: the operator waitlist sub-router is mounted at both /book/waitlist and /book/waitlist/ (apps/tenant-api/src/routes/reservations-operator.ts:76-84) and every non-root route is registered with both('/x') (reservations-waitlist.ts:100,141,204,241,276,307,339), so all 8 contract routes (architecture.md:1360: GET /, GET /quote, POST /, PATCH /:id, POST /:id/notify, /:id/seat, /:id/status, /reorder) answer both forms; the public waitlist surface uses bothForms() for all 6 routes (reservations-public-waitlist.ts:94,128,280,312,329,346,459) and the method-not-allowed guard also covers both forms (lines 490-500). I verified Hono's actual behaviour (v4.13.7 is strict by default: node_modules/hono/dist/hono-base.js:79-81 keeps the trailing slash; mergePath at utils/url.js:98-102 is what makes the double mount work) and that the duplicate registrations cannot double-execute a handler (compose only advances while a handler calls next(); the route handlers return a Response, rsvGuard awaits next() once). reservations-waitlist.test.ts:1109-1201 asserts the identical body for the sub-router root with and without slash, 201/200 on every slash form, and a 401 for a slash root with no token. (2) Schema alignment: packages/reservations/src/schemas/waitlist.ts now matches the DB enums exactly (7 statuses, channel walk_in|remote - tenant-db schema.ts:3067-3079), and every operator route imports the shared request schemas (reservations-waitlist.ts:1-12), as do the public join/notify-me routes (reservations-public-waitlist.ts:3-4,68-69); I checked both directions field by field against serializeWaitlistEntry (rsv-waitlist-service.ts:120-171), listWaitlistEntries (:194-226), getOperatorWaitlistQuote (:341-370), buildPublicWaitlistStatus (:991-1032) and the seat/conflict bodies (route lines 360-375; conflict() spreads details at the top level, lib/http.ts:96-108), and the tests parse real handler payloads (reservations-waitlist.test.ts:1203-1295). The App (waitlist-api.ts:1-14,178-218) and Sites (shared-schemas.test.ts:2-6,59-61) import the same schemas. (3) Occupied-table seat: createWalkIn now collects every overlapping occupancy and hands them to an onOccupied hook inside its transaction (rsv-booking-service.ts:1296-1334); waitlistOccupiedHandler answers 409 table_occupied with occupant/occupants/resolutions when no resolution is given, and resolves swap (unseat via assignReservationTables with an empty target, which sets assignment soft - rsv-booking-service.ts:1951-1975), move (explicit moveToTableIds or the same assignTables search the reservation reflow uses - rsv-waitlist-seat-resolution.ts:179-241) or overbook (walk-in overbook, reservation.overbook audited at rsv-booking-service.ts:1477) and audits waitlist.seat_resolution per occupant (rsv-waitlist-seat-resolution.ts:253-270). The hook runs inside the outer withReservationWrite transaction: assignReservationTables re-enters withReservationWrite and the active-context branch reuses the outer tx (lib/reservations-write.ts:717-736), so seat + occupant move + audit + day-version bump are one transaction; the DB trigger rsv_occupancy_no_overlap_insert (packages/tenant-db/drizzle/0016_reservations_foundation.sql:803-815) independently prevents an overlapping active non-overbook occupancy. Guest names are only fetched/returned when the token has READ_RESERVATION_GUEST (reservations-waitlist.ts:361, rsv-waitlist-seat-resolution.ts:38-56). Route tests cover 409/no-change, move (auto, explicit, no target rollback, locked rollback), swap (booked ok, seated refused), overbook (with/without reason), free-table no-op and unknown-resolution rejection (reservations-waitlist.test.ts:1297-1584); the App floor drop and seat dialog now offer exactly the resolutions the server names (floor-waitlist-panel.tsx:228-297, use-floor-waitlist.ts:77-121, added in 5e7c5b12), so VAL-WAIT-019's UI requirement is satisfied in the combined code. (4) areaPref: holdSchema accepts it (reservations-public.ts:204), createHold forwards it (line 477) and the engine search is restricted to a guest-selectable area (rsv-hold-service.ts:232-241 -> rsv-public-engine.ts:344-358 -> packages/reservations/src/engine/assign.ts:638); Sites sends slot.areaId (apps/sites/src/lib/reservations/flow.ts:652, api.ts:161-174) and the three route tests (reservations-public.test.ts:1487-1568) plus the Sites api test prove the held table is in the chosen area, that a full chosen area refuses even when another is free, and that unselectable/empty values fall back. No regression found in the reservation floor-plan drop (assignReservationTables untouched; the operator walk-in keeps its old 409 message and behaviour because only the waitlist seat passes onOccupied) or the public hold path (areaId null vs undefined is equivalent in the engine). Findings below are non-blocking; none blocks an expectedBehavior.

issues.description: Scope-ambiguity completeness note: the waitlist *settings* route (GET line 563 / PUT line 575, `/locations/:locationId/waitlist`, architecture.md:1390) has no trailing-slash variant, so `/operator/reservations/setup/locations/<id>/waitlist/` still 404s. The feature's item (1) targets the waitlist sub-router plus the public waitlist routes, and every one of those (8 operator + 6 public) is covered; no client or validation-contract assertion uses a trailing slash for the settings route (App calls it without one: apps/app/app/utils/reservations/waitlist-api.ts:255-278). Flagging only because the requirement says 'every waitlist operator route' and this path carries the waitlist feature flag.

Second import statement from './rsv-booking-service.ts' (the first is lines 21-24) violates the repo's documented `import/no-duplicates` convention (root AGENTS.md 'Duplicate Imports'). tenant-api has no lint script (apps/tenant-api/package.json has no `lint`) and oxlint did not flag it, so only a manual read catches it.

WAITLIST_SEAT_RESOLUTIONS is declared twice: here (used by the request/conflict Zod schemas) and again in apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-waitlist-seat-resolution.ts:19 (used by the service). The values agree today, but a future change to one would let the schema accept a resolution the service rejects (or vice versa). The service could import the shared constant instead.

The seat response's occupant `moves` are appended after createWalkIn returns, so they are not part of the value stored by the idempotency layer (createWalkIn's own `moves` array is always empty - rsv-booking-service.ts:1290,1502). A retry of the same seat with the same Idempotency-Key therefore replays `{entry, reservation, moves: []}` and silently loses the occupant move report the first call returned. Not user-visible today (the App floor-waitlist path ignores `moves`; only the reservation drop path renders move notices), but it is an inconsistency in the newly added response field.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Hono's strict trailing-slash behaviour is not recorded anywhere in library/ or AGENTS.md, yet it is the root cause of this fix and cost the worker three probe commands ('Probe Hono trailing slash behaviour', 'Probe double mount trailing slash', 'Probe empty path registration'). Hono defaults to strict (getPath keeps the trailing slash), so a route registered as '/x' does not answer '/x/'; the fix's pattern is a `both()` helper for leaf routes plus mounting a sub-router at both '/base' and '/base/'. A one-line note in library/engine-notes.md (or the tenant-api patterns file) would save the next worker the probing.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: node_modules/hono/dist/hono-base.js:79-81 (`this.getPath = strict ?? true ? options.getPath ?? getPath : getPathNoStrict`), node_modules/hono/dist/utils/url.js:98-102 (mergePath), the helpers at apps/tenant-api/src/routes/reservations-waitlist.ts:100 and reservations-public-waitlist.ts:94, and the double mount at reservations-operator.ts:76-84.

sharedStateObservations.observation: apps/app imports @repo/reservations from ~20 files but apps/app/package.json declares no such dependency (its @repo/* list stops at @repo/ui); this fix added another such import (waitlist-api.ts:1). apps/sites got the declaration when it adopted the shared schemas (apps/sites/package.json:49, commit 5e7c5b12). Resolution works today only because npm workspaces hoist the symlink into the root node_modules, so nothing fails, but the repo's dependency declarations do not describe the App's real graph and a strict workspace/lockfile step would break it. Worth one line in the mission notes or a one-line package.json fix.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The guest's chosen seating area is honoured when the hold's table is assigned, but not afterwards: createHold restricts the engine search by areaPref and stores the matched tables' occupancies, yet the hold row never records areaPrefId (rsvHolds.areaPrefId is written nowhere and read nowhere), and bookFromHold re-runs an unrestricted searchPublicDay (no areaId) and takes match.tableIds. So a hold in the guest-selected area can convert to a reservation on a table outside it. The feature's stated scope (hold endpoint + Sites client) is met and no validation-contract assertion covers the conversion, so this is recorded as knowledge for the validator, not as a defect of this feature.

summary: PASS. Commit 2c411941 delivers all four requested backend fixes and the combined code satisfies the feature's expectedBehavior. Trailing-slash coverage is complete for every waitlist route in the contract: the operator sub-router is mounted at both bases and all 8 of its routes answer both forms (reservations-waitlist.ts:100,141,204,241,276,307,339; reservations-operator.ts:76-84), and all 6 public waitlist/notify-me routes plus their method-not-allowed guards register both forms (reservations-public-waitlist.ts:94,128,280,312,329,346,459,490-500); tests assert identical answers and 401 on the slash root. The rewritten @repo/reservations waitlist/public schemas match the real route payloads in both directions (7 statuses, channel enum, operator request/response, seat response, 409 conflict body, public join/status/notify-me), and the tenant-api routes, the App client and the Sites contract test import them. The seat-on-occupied-table path returns 409 table_occupied with the occupant(s) and accepted resolutions, resolves swap/move/overbook by reusing assignReservationTables and assignTables inside the walk-in's single withReservationWrite transaction under the org lock, audits waitlist.seat_resolution per occupant and reservation.overbook for the overbook case, bumps the day version, and cannot double-book (the DB overlap trigger backstops it); tests cover all three resolutions plus rollback and guest-name redaction. The public hold honours areaPref only when the area is guest-selectable, and Sites sends the chosen slot's areaId. No regression in the reservation floor-plan drop path (untouched service; only the waitlist seat passes the new onOccupied hook) or the public hold path (null vs undefined areaId is equivalent). Four non-blocking findings: the waitlist settings route under /setup has no trailing-slash variant (outside the named scope, no caller uses it), a duplicate import from rsv-booking-service.ts, WAITLIST_SEAT_RESOLUTIONS duplicated between the schema and the service, and occupant `moves` missing on an idempotent seat replay. Four shared-state notes: Hono's strict trailing-slash behaviour is undocumented, the handoff's skillFeedback claims full procedure compliance although the transcript shows tests after implementation and no curl step, apps/app never declares @repo/reservations, and the hold's chosen area is not carried into the hold-to-book conversion.
